facts.statement: There are 7 continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America
Asia is the largest continent by both area and population
Australia is the smallest continent
There are 5 oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering more area than all the land on Earth combined
The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest ocean
Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent
Africa is the second-largest continent and contains 54 recognized countries
South America is the fourth-largest continent and contains 12 countries; Brazil is the largest by both area and population
Europe is the second-smallest continent by area but the third most populous, with about 44 countries
North America includes 23 countries and is the third-largest continent by area

common_errors.wrong: Africa is a country
common_errors.correct: Africa is a continent made up of 54 recognized countries

common_errors.wrong: There are 4 oceans
common_errors.correct: There are 5 oceans; the Southern Ocean was officially recognized by the International Hydrographic Organization

common_errors.wrong: Europe and Asia are separate landmasses
common_errors.correct: Europe and Asia share a continuous landmass called Eurasia but are considered separate continents culturally and historically

common_errors.wrong: Australia is just a country, not a continent
common_errors.correct: Australia is both a country and the world's smallest continent

facts.statement: The United States has 50 states
Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States and is not part of any state
The Mississippi River is the second-longest river in North America and flows from Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico
The Missouri River is the longest river in North America at approximately 2,341 miles
The five Great Lakes are Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, and Superior, remembered by the acronym HOMES
Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes by surface area and the largest freshwater lake by surface area in the world
The Rocky Mountains extend from Canada through the western United States to New Mexico
The Appalachian Mountains run along the eastern United States and are among the oldest mountains in the world
The Grand Canyon, carved by the Colorado River, is located in Arizona and is about 277 miles long and over a mile deep
The US is commonly divided into regions: Northeast, Southeast, Midwest, Southwest, and West

common_errors.wrong: Washington state is the capital of the United States
common_errors.correct: Washington, D.C. (District of Columbia) is the U.S. capital; Washington state is in the Pacific Northwest

common_errors.wrong: The Mississippi is the longest river in North America
common_errors.correct: The Missouri River is slightly longer than the Mississippi; however, the Mississippi-Missouri river system combined is the longest in North America

common_errors.wrong: There are 52 states in the United States
common_errors.correct: There are 50 states in the United States; Washington, D.C. and Puerto Rico are not states

common_errors.wrong: Alaska is a small state because it looks small on many maps
common_errors.correct: Alaska is the largest U.S. state by area; it appears smaller on many map projections due to distortion

facts.statement: China and India are the two most populous countries in the world, each with over 1.4 billion people
Russia is the largest country in the world by area, spanning across Europe and Asia
Canada is the second-largest country by area, and its capital is Ottawa
The top five most populous countries are India, China, the United States, Indonesia, and Pakistan
The five largest countries by area are Russia, Canada, the United States, China, and Brazil
Beijing is the capital of China, and New Delhi is the capital of India
Brasilia is the capital of Brazil, not Rio de Janeiro or Sao Paulo
Tokyo, the capital of Japan, is one of the most populous metropolitan areas in the world

common_errors.wrong: Sydney is the capital of Australia
common_errors.correct: Canberra is the capital of Australia; Sydney is the largest city

common_errors.wrong: Rio de Janeiro is the capital of Brazil
common_errors.correct: Brasilia has been the capital of Brazil since 1960; Rio de Janeiro is a major city but not the capital

common_errors.wrong: Istanbul is the capital of Turkey
common_errors.correct: Ankara is the capital of Turkey; Istanbul is the largest city and former capital

common_errors.wrong: Holland and the Netherlands are different countries
common_errors.correct: Holland refers to two provinces (North Holland and South Holland) within the Netherlands; they are not separate countries

facts.statement: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level at 29,032 feet (8,849 meters), located in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and Tibet
K2 is the second-tallest mountain above sea level at 28,251 feet (8,611 meters), located on the China-Pakistan border
Mount Kilimanjaro is the tallest mountain in Africa at 19,341 feet (5,895 meters) and is a dormant volcano in Tanzania
The Nile River is the longest river in the world at approximately 4,130 miles (6,650 km), flowing through northeastern Africa
The Amazon River carries more water than any other river in the world and flows through South America
The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of northern Africa
The Yangtze River is the longest river in Asia and the third-longest in the world at approximately 3,917 miles (6,300 km)
Greenland is the largest island in the world (Australia is classified as a continent rather than an island)

common_errors.wrong: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain measured from base to peak
common_errors.correct: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller from base to peak at about 33,500 feet (10,210 meters), but most of it is underwater; Everest has the highest elevation above sea level

common_errors.wrong: The Sahara is the largest desert in the world
common_errors.correct: The Antarctic Desert is the largest desert overall at about 5.5 million square miles; the Sahara is the largest hot desert at about 3.6 million square miles

common_errors.wrong: The Amazon is the longest river in the world
common_errors.correct: The Nile is generally considered the longest river at approximately 4,130 miles; the Amazon is the largest by water volume

common_errors.wrong: Mount Kilimanjaro is in South America
common_errors.correct: Mount Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania, East Africa; it is the tallest mountain on the African continent

facts.statement: The five major climate zones are tropical, dry (arid), temperate, continental, and polar
The equator is an imaginary line at 0 degrees latitude that divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres
The Tropic of Cancer is at approximately 23.5 degrees north latitude, and the Tropic of Capricorn is at approximately 23.5 degrees south latitude
The Arctic Circle is at approximately 66.5 degrees north latitude, and the Antarctic Circle is at approximately 66.5 degrees south latitude
Tropical climates are found near the equator and are warm year-round with significant rainfall
The rain shadow effect occurs when mountains block moist air, causing the leeward side to be dry
Polar climates are found near the North and South Poles and experience extremely cold temperatures year-round
Temperate climates have moderate temperatures with distinct seasons and are found in the mid-latitudes between the tropics and polar regions
Continental climates have large temperature ranges between summer and winter and are typically found in the interior of large landmasses
Ocean currents affect climate: the Gulf Stream carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico to western Europe, keeping it warmer than other regions at the same latitude

common_errors.wrong: The equator passes through the United States
common_errors.correct: The equator does not pass through the United States; it runs through countries like Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Kenya, and Indonesia

common_errors.wrong: Deserts are always hot
common_errors.correct: Deserts are defined by low precipitation, not temperature; Antarctica is a cold desert and the largest desert in the world

common_errors.wrong: Tropical climates only exist in Africa
common_errors.correct: Tropical climates are found near the equator on every inhabited continent, including parts of South America, Central America, Southeast Asia, and Oceania

common_errors.wrong: Seasons are caused by the distance between Earth and the Sun
common_errors.correct: Seasons are caused by the tilt of Earth's axis (23.5 degrees), not by distance from the Sun. When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it is summer there

facts.statement: Latitude lines run east-west and measure distance north or south of the equator (0 degrees latitude)
Longitude lines run north-south and measure distance east or west of the Prime Meridian (0 degrees longitude)
The equator is at 0 degrees latitude and divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres
The Prime Meridian is at 0 degrees longitude and passes through Greenwich, England, dividing the Earth into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres
A compass rose shows the cardinal directions: north, south, east, and west
A map scale shows the relationship between distances on the map and actual distances on Earth
A map legend (or key) explains the symbols, colors, and lines used on a map
The four hemispheres are Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western

common_errors.wrong: Latitude lines run north-south
common_errors.correct: Latitude lines run east-west (horizontally) and measure how far north or south a location is from the equator

common_errors.wrong: Longitude lines run east-west
common_errors.correct: Longitude lines run north-south (vertically) and measure how far east or west a location is from the Prime Meridian

common_errors.wrong: The Prime Meridian divides the Northern and Southern Hemispheres
common_errors.correct: The equator divides the Northern and Southern Hemispheres; the Prime Meridian divides the Eastern and Western Hemispheres

common_errors.wrong: North is always at the top of every map
common_errors.correct: While most modern maps place north at the top by convention, maps can be oriented in any direction and historically have been

facts.statement: A volcano is an opening in Earth's crust through which lava, ash, and gases erupt
A peninsula is a piece of land surrounded by water on three sides, such as Florida or the Italian Peninsula
An isthmus is a narrow strip of land connecting two larger land areas, such as the Isthmus of Panama connecting North and South America
An archipelago is a chain or group of islands, such as the Hawaiian Islands, the Philippines, or Indonesia
A plateau is a flat, elevated area of land, sometimes called a tableland; the Tibetan Plateau is the highest and largest in the world
A canyon is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides carved by a river, such as the Grand Canyon
A delta is a landform created by sediment deposited at the mouth of a river, such as the Nile Delta or Mississippi Delta
A fjord is a long, narrow inlet with steep cliffs created by glacial erosion, commonly found in Norway
A mesa is a flat-topped hill with steep sides, common in the American Southwest; it is smaller than a plateau
A butte is a smaller, narrower version of a mesa with steep sides and a flat top

common_errors.wrong: All mountains are volcanoes
common_errors.correct: Mountains can form through tectonic plate collisions, faulting, and folding; only some mountains are volcanoes

common_errors.wrong: A strait and an isthmus are the same thing
common_errors.correct: A strait is a narrow body of water between two landmasses; an isthmus is a narrow strip of land between two bodies of water -- they are opposites

common_errors.wrong: Valleys are only formed by rivers
common_errors.correct: Valleys can also be formed by glaciers (U-shaped valleys), tectonic activity, and erosion

facts.statement: The world population is approximately 8 billion people
Tokyo, Japan is one of the most populous metropolitan areas in the world with over 37 million people in its greater metro area
Urbanization is the process of people moving from rural areas to cities, and more than half of the world's population now lives in urban areas
Migration is the movement of people from one place to another, which can be voluntary or forced
Population density measures how many people live in a given area, usually expressed as people per square mile or square kilometer
Asia is the most populous continent, home to about 60 percent of the world's population
Other highly populous cities include Delhi, Shanghai, Sao Paulo, Mexico City, Cairo, and Mumbai
A megalopolis is a chain of closely linked metropolitan areas, such as the US Northeast corridor from Boston to Washington, D.C.

common_errors.wrong: The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye
common_errors.correct: The Great Wall of China is not visible from space with the naked eye; it is too narrow despite being very long

common_errors.wrong: Most of the world's population lives in rural areas
common_errors.correct: Since around 2007, more than half of the world's population lives in urban areas, and that share continues to grow

common_errors.wrong: China is the most populous country in the world
common_errors.correct: India surpassed China as the most populous country around 2023, with both countries having populations over 1.4 billion

facts.statement: The capital of California is Sacramento, not Los Angeles or San Francisco
The capital of New York is Albany, not New York City
The capital of Texas is Austin, not Houston or Dallas
The capital of Florida is Tallahassee, not Miami or Orlando
The capital of Illinois is Springfield, not Chicago
The capital of Pennsylvania is Harrisburg, not Philadelphia or Pittsburgh
The capital of Georgia is Atlanta
The capital of Ohio is Columbus
The capital of Michigan is Lansing, not Detroit
The capital of Massachusetts is Boston
Alaska is the largest US state by area but one of the least populated
Rhode Island is the smallest US state by area
Hawaii is the only US state that is entirely made up of islands and is located in the Pacific Ocean

common_errors.wrong: New York City is the capital of New York
common_errors.correct: Albany is the capital of New York state; New York City is the largest city but not the capital

common_errors.wrong: Los Angeles is the capital of California
common_errors.correct: Sacramento is the capital of California; Los Angeles is the most populous city in the state

common_errors.wrong: Chicago is the capital of Illinois
common_errors.correct: Springfield is the capital of Illinois; Chicago is the largest city and is in the northeastern part of the state

common_errors.wrong: Miami is the capital of Florida
common_errors.correct: Tallahassee is the capital of Florida; Miami is a major city in southeastern Florida

common_errors.wrong: Detroit is the capital of Michigan
common_errors.correct: Lansing is the capital of Michigan; Detroit is the largest city

facts.statement: London is the capital of the United Kingdom and England
Paris is the capital of France and is known as the City of Light
Berlin is the capital of Germany
Moscow is the capital of Russia and is the largest city in Europe by population
Cairo is the capital of Egypt and is the largest city in Africa
Nairobi is the capital of Kenya
Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina
Seoul is the capital of South Korea
Bangkok is the capital of Thailand
Rome is the capital of Italy and was the center of the ancient Roman Empire
Madrid is the capital of Spain
Mexico City is the capital of Mexico and one of the most populous cities in the world

common_errors.wrong: Mumbai is the capital of India
common_errors.correct: New Delhi is the capital of India; Mumbai is the largest city by population

common_errors.wrong: Toronto is the capital of Canada
common_errors.correct: Ottawa is the capital of Canada; Toronto is the largest city

common_errors.wrong: Shanghai is the capital of China
common_errors.correct: Beijing is the capital of China; Shanghai is the largest city by population

common_errors.wrong: Lagos is the capital of Nigeria
common_errors.correct: Abuja has been the capital of Nigeria since 1991; Lagos is the largest city

facts.statement: The major land biomes include tropical rainforest, temperate forest, desert, grassland, tundra, and taiga (boreal forest)
Tropical rainforests are found near the equator and contain more species of plants and animals than any other biome
The tundra biome is found in Arctic regions and is characterized by permafrost, very cold temperatures, and low-growing vegetation
The taiga (boreal forest) is the largest land biome, stretching across Canada, Russia, and Scandinavia, dominated by coniferous trees
Renewable resources can be replenished naturally, such as solar energy, wind, and timber; nonrenewable resources like coal, oil, and natural gas cannot
The Amazon Rainforest is the largest tropical rainforest in the world, covering much of the Amazon River basin in South America
Savannas are tropical grasslands with scattered trees, found in Africa, South America, and Australia
Deforestation is the clearing of forests for agriculture, logging, or development, and it contributes to habitat loss and climate change

common_errors.wrong: the tundra has many tall trees
common_errors.correct: The tundra has no trees because of permafrost and extreme cold; vegetation is limited to mosses, lichens, and small shrubs

common_errors.wrong: all deserts are hot and sandy
common_errors.correct: Deserts are defined by low precipitation; they can be hot (Sahara) or cold (Antarctica, Gobi). Many deserts have rocky terrain, not sand

common_errors.wrong: the rainforest is shrinking but it does not affect the rest of the world
common_errors.correct: Rainforests absorb carbon dioxide and produce oxygen; their destruction affects global climate, biodiversity, and weather patterns worldwide

facts.statement: The Mediterranean Sea is bordered by Europe, Africa, and Asia, and is connected to the Atlantic Ocean through the Strait of Gibraltar
The Caspian Sea is the largest enclosed body of water on Earth, bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan
The Dead Sea, between Israel and Jordan, is one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth and the lowest point on land at about 1,412 feet below sea level
The Gulf of Mexico is a large body of water bordered by the United States, Mexico, and Cuba
The Caribbean Sea is located between Central America, South America, and the Caribbean islands
Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest and oldest freshwater lake in the world, holding about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater
The Danube River is the second-longest river in Europe, flowing through 10 countries from Germany to the Black Sea
Niagara Falls is located on the border between the United States (New York) and Canada (Ontario)

common_errors.wrong: the Caspian Sea is an ocean
common_errors.correct: Despite its name and large size, the Caspian Sea is an enclosed lake — the world's largest — not an ocean or true sea

common_errors.wrong: the Dead Sea is a freshwater lake
common_errors.correct: The Dead Sea is extremely salty (about 10 times saltier than the ocean), making it nearly impossible for most organisms to survive in it

common_errors.wrong: all large bodies of water are called oceans
common_errors.correct: Large bodies of water include oceans, seas, gulfs, bays, and lakes — each has different characteristics based on size, salinity, and connection to other waters

common_errors.wrong: the Great Lakes contain salt water
common_errors.correct: The Great Lakes are freshwater lakes. They contain approximately 21% of the world's surface freshwater
